"},{"id":"9:44","text":"Review and provenance
The supplied smartphone concept is Reference A, irrespective of attachment order. Four physical-camera photographs inform the ivory plastic, concentric lens ribs, metal trim, flash flutes, sloped ledge and dark film compartment. No official camera logos are used. Original Check2GO PNG from the reference commit is imported without changing proportions (1200:209).
Retained hierarchy: brand upper-left; flash upper-right; large central circular preview; red shutter left; flash and switch right; counter/timer left; spectrum below lens; InstantRoom above slot; Gallery / Photo Booth / Settings below.
Intentional deviations: reduced lens diameter to accommodate 48-unit controls; reduced perspective and material effects for native rendering; no decorative physical phone bezel; system-safe margins; cartridge replacement via counter and corkboard via Gallery. The circular view uses a generated photographic park sample, not a real capture. Two Figma AI image generations were used, including a corrected full-bleed source image; all housing and controls remain native editable layers.
The file now contains all ten requested pages plus a dedicated review-prototype page. Professional Full access was verified.

Resolve in order: global primitives → semantic app roles → camera family → physical finish → film presentation. App appearance never modifies physical finish; neither changes image processing, film selection or photo pixels.
Global semantics: surface/text/border/disabled/focus/error/warning. Light: #FFF9EF / #242526 / #777571. Dark: #17191A / #FFF9EF / #BDB8AF. Disabled foreground #777571 at full opacity with disabled label; decorative opacity 0.4 only. Focus #007C91 on cream; light focus #7EDCEA on charcoal. Error #B3261E and warning #805400 on cream; dark error #FFB4AB and warning #FFDCA7.
Camera physical tokens: cream #EDE5D8, charcoal #242526, mechanical gray #777571, shutter #E32A1C, metal #BDB8AF, paper #FFF9EF, ready indicator #287A4A, ready text #216B3E, brand blue #0064BA, brand teal #00A89D. Proposed spectrum: #D50063 / #F27916 / #F5CF20 / #388842 / #008CB5. This spectrum intentionally interprets the concept and requires approval because the baseline uses a different four-color decorative spectrum. Original finish mappings remain in finishes.json.
All opaque colors have RGBA alpha 1; tokens.json supplies explicit numeric channels. Shadow rgba(0,0,0,0.32), highlight rgba(255,255,255,0.42), grain rgba(255,255,255,0.035), scrim rgba(0,0,0,0.60).
"},{"id":"9:52","text":"Typography and assets
Proposed interface font: Inter Regular/Bold, not claimed to match baseline Roboto. Product wordmark: Inter Bold Italic24/30 in proposal. Product approval required for typography change. Labels12/16 minimum; counter24/28 tabular; body16/24; secondary14/20; title24/30; instructions18/26. Dynamic Type/font scaling may increase settings rows and sheet heights; compact engraved labels get equivalent accessibility labels and never carry sole instructions.
Baseline fonts exist: sol_kol.ttf, denistina.ttf, historic.ttf (see source assets). ASSETS.md confirms Sol Kol OFL1.1, retained in assets/licenses/Sol-Kol-OFL.txt. Denistina and Historic redistribution not independently verified. Do not repackage those two fonts into new design asset distributions pending rights confirmation. Caption font choices retain exact labels. The caption screen includes an actual Sol Kol outlined specimen, generated from the bundled OFL font. It is editable as vectors; changing the caption as native Figma text requires installing the font. Denistina/Historic previews remain blocked by rights verification. Caption limit80 Unicode code points and2 lines, explicit validation, no silent truncation.
Asset inventory: supplied Check2GO logo (PNG, keep transparent); native shell, ribs, flash glass, ejection roller, pushpin and paper geometry; vector sample scene; primitive color tokens; original finish table. Original font binaries are deliberately excluded from this review bundle. UI icons should be original 24×24 vectors: archive as stacked prints; booth as four-cell strip; gear as 8-tooth settings; bolt with off slash; timer circle+hand; switch as camera+two directional arrows; pin as head+stem; cartridge as tray. Camera timer, flash, switch and navigation now use original native vectors; six SVGs are exported in assets/. Archive/corkboard action icons beyond this core set remain specified rather than fully exported.

Shutter: Idle / Pressed / Capturing / Disabled / Timer active / Photo Booth active. Press depth2, cap scale0.97; enabled only on ready camera with exposure available. Timer/booth state shows remaining time/shot index. Busy blocks repeat capture. Stop/cancel remains separately reachable. Screen reader: Take photo; disabled reason; countdown announcements, not per-frame speech.
Lens: live / focusing / focused / failed / permission denied / unavailable. Focus guide white; active ring teal; failed indicator labeled Try again. Permission state includes Open Settings and Back. Switching freezes previous frame briefly with cover, never flips the preview as a 3D card.
Flash: off / on / charging / ready / firing / unavailable. Bolt retained throughout300ms toggle; off uses slash, charging uses progress arc, ready adds labeled green status, unavailable uses disabled reason. Front screen flash and border illumination must follow existing front-camera behavior; hardware availability governs rear flash.
Counter:10 full;9–2 partial;1 warning text;0 empty with Replace cartridge action. No automatic replacement. Disabled shutter at0; cartridge replacement confirmation required if unused exposures exist. Counter resets10 only after successful load completion.
Timer selector: Off /5s /15s /30s, selected radio state and confirmation. Photo Booth: four photos, five-second intervals; verify>=4 available shots before start. Outputs2×2 sheet or1×4 strip; explicit Cancel explains already-used exposures. No rollback of consumed shots.
Photo frame: undeveloped / partial / completed / pinned / selected. Paper ratio comes from film. Caption/editor, export/share, remove and pin actions apply only where current app allows them. Gallery accesses corkboard via Board button. Corkboard: unpin before dragging or rotating, matching the source Placement.move behavior. Two-finger rotate and accessible move/rotate menu are gesture alternatives. Re-pin after arranging. Pushpin tap selects photo; removal confirmation only when removal would delete data (unpin alone reversible).
Generic controls: default/pressed/focus/disabled/loading/error; 48 target; label property; icon property; surface and state tokens. Sheets: drag handle, title, close, scroll region, safe-area footer; modal blocks background focus. Empty archive: No photographs yet + Take your first photo. Error: Camera unavailable + Retry; preserve existing photos. Loading never displays indefinite progress without a cancel/back path.
The component library now has 85 variants across the shutter and 22 additional state families, six reusable icon components, two shell/preview components, four full-camera finish variants and four physical film formats. Eight core controls/preview elements in each camera layout are instances. Physical body finish is bound to its own variable collection; application appearance has independent Light/Dark modes. Remaining manual material details are intentionally fixed geometry.

## Manual cartridge replacement

Closed → confirmation → Open → Removed → Inserted → Closed. The initial example contains 10 unused exposures. The confirmation names the exact 10 exposures to be discarded. Cancel before confirmation preserves the cartridge. After confirmation, the prototype asks the user to complete the manual loading sequence before returning to capture. Removing or inserting a cartridge must not reset the counter. Reset to exactly10 only after successful compartment closure and load completion.

Reusable native component: Cartridge compartment / manual phases, component set43:389, four phases Closed/Open/Removed/Inserted. Prototype phase frames36:1291,36:1307,36:1324,36:1337. Warning confirmation36:1353. Saved-photo data is independent of cartridge changes.

The example uses Classic / Classic Color to isolate the loading state machine; film-format and treatment selection are not implemented as persistent preferences in this prototype. Native implementation must preserve the selected film and treatment and use their source-authoritative dimensions. If native navigation leaves an unfinished loading flow, persist its partial phase and block capture until closure; do not silently refill a cartridge. The prototype hides its explicit Back button after confirmation and does not simulate operating-system back gestures or lifecycle interruptions.

## Self-timer

Off/5s/15s/30s each lead to a camera showing the chosen preset. Changing the preset does not consume an exposure. Pressing the shutter starts a countdown; Cancel returns to the camera with that same preset. The five-second demonstration shows5→4→3→2→1, one second per frame, then capture. The15/30-second demonstrations retain the correct total delay but show only the starting numeral and the final second; intermediate numerals are not modeled. They do not imply that only two ticks occur in the actual application. Each long preset has its own final-second frame so Cancel preserves the original preset.

Timer menu36:1379; selected states36:1388/36:1541/36:1702/36:1863. One exposure is consumed only on an accepted capture, never when changing a preset, waiting or cancelling. The Figma prototype illustrates a bounded capture scenario; it does not maintain the application's exposure ledger across all navigation paths. Production countdown uses the existing app clock and emits accessible announcements at an appropriate cadence, not per animation frame.

## Camera finish selection

Four dedicated selection screens show White, Black, Red Accent and Cream / Spectrum. Tapping an unselected swatch updates the selected outline, label and actual full camera thumbnail. Tapping the already-selected swatch leaves the screen unchanged. Use this finish opens the matching full camera; opening Settings from that camera returns to its matching finish selector.

Selectors39:1919/39:2117/39:2316/39:2514. Resulting cameras18:685/18:863/18:1042/18:1220. Body colors use the source-authoritative modes already defined in revision2. Application appearance, film format, image processing and photo colors remain independent. This is frame-based state demonstration; it does not persist settings across every unrelated route or restart.

## Recovery states

Camera access request: explain the reason, offer the native permission request and allow browsing saved photos. The prototype's Allow camera action is explicitly labeled as a demonstration and does not request device permissions. A production denial must lead to the platform-appropriate Settings explanation rather than repeatedly prompting.

Camera unavailable: show a possible camera-in-use cause without asserting an unverified technical error; offer Retry and Browse saved photos. Preserve cartridge accounting and saved photographs during recovery.

Save failure: propose a retry path that retains the captured image and never forces another exposure. Retaining a retryable image is an implementation requirement, not a verified claim about current0.5.0 behavior. Development must confirm the actual capture/persistence boundary and storage-full handling before approving this design for release. The prototype routes Retry to a sample archive and does not write data.
